To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the renormalization of energy-momentum tensors in scalar and gauge theories is completely determined in terms of the renormalization group functions and the renormalized mass of the elementary spin-zero particles.
the energy-momentum operator is not renormalized and that the energy-mass density is renormalized by the same amount as the energy-mass of a particle.
the energy-momentum operator of a quantum field theory has a finite expectation value in the presence of an external gravitational field.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the energy-momentum tensors in quantum field theory, and with the problem of finding the correct renormalized form of this tensor.
the energy-momentum density of a quantum field theory.
the renormalization properties of the energy momentum tensor in quantum field theory and the renormalization of composite fields.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy-momentum tensors of ϕ4 theory, spontaneously broken Yang-Mills theories and the standard model, are renormalizable and finite in the sense that the divergences of the Green's functions of θμν and the matter fields can be absorbed by a finite number of renormalizations of parameters in the Lagrangians.
all the divergences are absorbed into the counterterms of the Lagrangian and into the renormalization of a single parameter of the improvement term.
the energy-momentum of a quantum system is finite to all orders in the perturbation theory of ϕ4 theory or spontaneously broken non-abelian gauge field theories.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the energy-momentum tensors in scalar and non-Abelian vector field theories have the same structure as in the case of the electromagnetic field, i.e. they are given by a sum of a symmetric part, which is the energy-momentum density, and an antisymmetric part, which is a current density of angular momentum.
, to all orders in the coupling constants, the energy-momentum density of the fields in the vacuum is finite.
the energy-momentum density of the vacuum in the presence of an external field is not zero, but is given by the vacuum expectation value of the Callan–Coleman–Jackiw improvement term.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the energy-momentum density of the quantum vacuum is not infinite.
the energy-momentum tensors in scalar and non-Abelian Yang-Mills theories are finite to all orders in the perturbation expansion, provided that the Callan-Colemnan-Jackiw improvement is included.

the renormalized energy-momentum tensor is finite to all orders in the perturbative expansion, and that the Callan-Coley-Jackiw term in θμ is not a renormalized field, as is sometimes thought, but a renormalization counterterm.
